sections.h2: Where is the Gaston County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The office is on the first floor of the Gaston County Courthouse at 325 Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Way, Gastonia, NC 28052. That address was formerly listed as 325 N. Marietta Street, so older deeds, letters and directions may still show the old street name.

Mail goes to P.O. Box 1578, Gastonia, NC 28053, and the phone is 704-862-7681. The office is open from 8:30 am to 5 pm. Real estate recordings are accepted until 4:45 pm, which is earlier than closing time, so a late-afternoon closing in Gastonia, Belmont, Mount Holly or Cherryville needs to be sent in with room to spare. No appointment is needed to use the records or to take a notary oath.

sections.h2: What changed in Gaston County's online records search?
sections.html:
The office switched to a new records vendor on Thursday, May 28, 2026, and the old system has been retired. The county says every record from the old system is now in the new one, so bookmarks and links that pointed to the old site need updating.

The public search is the place to look for deeds, deeds of trust and other property records. Some older records are not online, and the county asks you to visit or call for help with those. Uncertified copies can be pulled online. For a certified copy you can use the county's Certified Copy Request Portal, call 704-862-7681, email rod@gastongov.com or go to the office. A seller who needs a prior deed to prove how the family took title will usually want a certified copy for the closing attorney.

sections.h2: What does a deed copy cost in Gaston County?
sections.html:
A black and white copy is $0.25 a page, and a certified copy is $5 for the first page and $2 for each additional page, according to the office's FAQ.

The office takes cash, business checks, money orders, debit and credit for its fees, and checks or money orders are made out to Gaston County Register of Deeds. Staff can show you the books and help with the computers, but title research by Register of Deeds employees is prohibited by law, and the office does not check liens for you. If you lost your deed, you can buy a copy in person or request one in writing at the P.O. Box. To change names on a deed, a new deed has to be drawn up, and the office advises seeing an attorney because it keeps no legal forms for deeds or powers of attorney.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Gaston County?
sections.html:
Gaston County charges the uniform statewide fees in G.S. 161-10, and the county's FAQ points to that schedule for the cost of recording a deed or power of attorney.

  • General instruments: $26.00 for the first 15 pages, then $4.00 per added page.
  • Deeds of trust and mortgages: $64.00 for the first 35 pages, then $4.00 per added page.
  • Satisfactions and cancellations of a deed of trust: no fee.
  • Plats: $21.00 per sheet.
  • Several instruments in one document: $10.00 for each additional instrument.

The deed excise tax is separate. G.S. 105-228.30 sets it at $1.00 on each $500.00 or fractional part of the price or value, and the seller pays it before recording. The office collects it with the recording fee.

sections.h2: Can Gaston County help protect me from deed and lien fraud?
sections.html:
Yes. The office partners with the county's land records software provider to offer a free notification service. You sign up with a name and an email address, and you are alerted when a recording is filed in your name.

The county is clear that no system can prevent fraud. The alerts are meant to help you spot a bad filing quickly, which matters if you own a vacant, inherited or rental house in Gaston County and might not see the mail. Anyone who prepares a document for recording is also barred from including Social Security, bank account, card or similar numbers unless the law requires it. If one does appear, you can ask in writing for it to be removed from the online image under G.S. 132-1.10(g). There is no fee for that request, though the underlying filing stays in the public record.

sections.h2: How do Gaston County property values and appeals tie to a sale?
sections.html:
The county reappraises on a four-year cycle. The last reappraisal took effect January 1, 2023, and the next countywide one is scheduled for 2027, with an informal review step before the Board of Equalization and Review meets.

Appeals run from January 1 until the board adjourns, which the county says is typically the last week of April, or the later of the adjournment or 30 days from a Notice of Value Change. The property tax office is at 128 West Main Avenue in Gastonia, phone 704-866-3158. Property taxes are a separate bill from anything the Register of Deeds charges, and they follow the owner of record, so a buyer will expect the seller to settle the year's tax at closing. Our Gaston County property tax guide covers rates, relief programs and payment options in detail.

sections.h2: What recording rule do sellers in Gaston County need to know?
sections.html:
A transfer or lease of more than three years is effective against lien creditors and purchasers for value only once it is registered in the county where the land sits, and the order of registration sets priority (G.S. 47-18).

That is why a seller should confirm that earlier deeds in the chain, any estate documents and any release of a paid-off loan are on record before a new buyer's deed goes in. Satisfactions cost nothing to record. Ask your closing attorney to search the index and to send the satisfaction of your old mortgage so the title is clear on the day you sell.

sections.h2: What should an heir of a Gaston County house record before selling?
sections.html:
Start with the estate paperwork, because a deed signed by someone who does not yet hold title will not clear. When a person dies without a will and the personal property is modest, an heir can use the small estate affidavit procedure in G.S. 28A-25-1, which is filed with the clerk of superior court in the county where the decedent lived and which describes each tract of real property the person owned.

That statute caps personal property, less liens, at $20,000, or up to $30,000 for a sole-heir surviving spouse after allowances, and it requires waiting 30 days after the date of death with no petition for a personal representative pending. Whatever route applies, the document that gives you authority to sell ends up in the Register of Deeds index in Gastonia, so allow time for it before the buyer's closing date.

sections.h2: Does a land contract have to be recorded in Gaston County?
sections.html:
For a seller-financed contract for deed on a one to four family home or manufactured home, North Carolina's Chapter 47H requires the seller to record the contract, or a memorandum of it, within five business days.

The chapter applies to agreements with five or more payments after the down payment where the seller keeps title and the price is $5,000 or more. The purchaser may cancel until midnight of the third business day after signing. Forfeiture needs a written notice of default giving at least 30 days to cure. If you hold or are buying on such a contract in Gaston County, confirm with the office or an attorney that the recorded memorandum is in the index before you rely on it in a sale.

faqs.q: Where do I mail documents to the Gaston County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Mail them to Gaston County Register of Deeds, P.O. Box 1578, Gastonia, NC 28053. For overnight service the county suggests an express envelope with a prepaid return envelope enclosed.

faqs.q: What is the cutoff for recording a deed in Gaston County?
faqs.a: Real estate recordings are accepted until 4:45 pm. The office itself is open from 8:30 am to 5 pm, and marriage applications stop at 4:30 pm.

faqs.q: How much is a certified copy of a deed in Gaston County?
faqs.a: A certified copy costs $5 for the first page and $2 for each additional page. A plain black and white copy is $0.25 a page.

faqs.q: Is the Gaston County records search online?
faqs.a: Yes. The county moved to a new public search system on May 28, 2026, with the old system's records carried over. Some older records are not digitized, so call 704-862-7681 for help.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on a Gaston County sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays the excise tax, at $1.00 per $500.00 of the price or fraction of that amount, before the deed is recorded. Your settlement statement shows the figure.
